summary: I read all 3,184 lines of sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/ end to end, inventoried every numeric constant and every declared vocabulary, and cross-checked each against the 17 completed live runs in artifacts/simulations_v3 and artifacts/matched_pairs. On the central claim I can give a clean pass: there is no scenario router, no capability menu, no fixed social-action vocabulary, no branch keyed on a name/topic/domain/question type, and no forbidden statistical construct anywhere in the runtime or the kernel it uses - and, most importantly, no arbitrary numerical variable controls social behaviour. Every one of the 15 comparisons in trajectory.py is a clock ordering, a change-detector, a cardinality test, or a counter against a technical ceiling; nine distinct social questions across seven domains ran through byte-identical code (RUNTIME_FREEZE.txt reproduced with git hash-object, 13/13 OK). It fails on the bloat half: WAKE_PROVENANCE declares five members and only two are reachable from any code path, the missing 'known_deadline' is the only declared mechanism that would bring a person back because a deadline is approaching, and six trace kinds - precisely the ones recording where code overrode the model - are emitted into the Trace and persisted to nothing.

findings.title: WAKE_PROVENANCE declares five kinds of wake; only two are reachable, and the missing 'known_deadline' is the mechanism that would keep a run alive to its horizon
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:154-158 declares ("actor_plan", "observed_event", "world_process", "known_deadline", "action_completion"). _schedule_wake (trajectory.py:185) is called from exactly two sites in the whole runtime: :368 passing provenance="world_process" and :498 passing provenance="actor_plan". No code path ever passes "observed_event", "known_deadline" or "action_completion". Confirmed empirically: across every grounded_wakes.jsonl in artifacts/simulations_v3 and artifacts/matched_pairs (17 completed runs, 183 wakes) only world_process and actor_plan ever appear. Consequence in the corpus: artifacts/simulations_v3/case1_cold_email - steps=1, one committed event (e11, Jordan sends the cold email), the world's own judgment says the email is 'in transit to Mark Cuban's email server' and schedules a world_process wake to 'Check if the email has arrived in Mark Cuban's inbox'; that wake fires at 14:01, journal.available_unobserved('mark_cuban') is empty so the world is never asked, Mark is consulted with an empty view (c8: 'I have no current tasks or observations'), volunteers no next_wake, the queue empties, trajectory.py:825-834 breaks, and finish() jumps 14 days to answer NO_AT_CUTOFF. artifacts/matched_pairs/b1_okafor_herrera__r3 is the same shape: steps=1, 1 event, NO_AT_CUTOFF. Two artifacts validate against the full five-member set and therefore can never notice this: evaluation/verify_run.py:20-21 ('The five kinds of reason a wake is allowed to exist for') and tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:1401-1403, which asserts only membership.
findings.why_it_matters: Two of the three unreachable names ('observed_event', 'action_completion') do at least exist as behaviour - they are implemented as immediate actor_step calls at trajectory.py:594 and :666 rather than as scheduled wakes - so for those the label is dead documentation. 'known_deadline' is different: nothing anywhere in the runtime ever brings a person back to a situation because a deadline they know about is close. Since the main loop terminates the instant the queue is empty and the only two live wake sources are an actor volunteering next_wake and the world volunteering one, a run in which neither happens stops at step 1 and the closing judgment then answers NO over a fortnight that was never simulated. That is a budget/plumbing artifact being reported as a social answer, and it is invisible to both the acceptance checker and the test suite because both validate against the aspirational five-member set.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire known_deadline - schedule one wake per actor at a code-derived offset before the cutoff carried in bindings, with provenance='known_deadline' - or delete the three unreachable members from trajectory.py:154-158, evaluation/verify_run.py:20-21 and the test, so the declared vocabulary is exactly what the code can produce.

findings.title: Six trace kinds are emitted and persisted nowhere - and they are exactly the moments where a code constant overrode the model
findings.evidence: trajectory.py emits note("event_abandoned") :305, note("duplicate_event_dropped") :330, note("duration_floored") :347, note("actor_turn_abandoned") :466, note("group_observation_split") :855, note("progression_skipped") :906. trace.write_artifacts (trace.py:38-105) persists only actor_view, world_judgment, terminal_check, terminal_verification, continuity_review, actor_response_rejected, event_review, event_rejected, wake_scheduled; render_trajectory (trace.py:126-178) renders only actor_decision, actor_view, committed_event, event_beyond_cutoff, item_observed, terminal_check, world_judgment. None of the six appear in any of the 21 artifacts. What is therefore unauditable in the corpus: 9 abandoned turns (a1_responsive__r2, a2_unresponsive__r3, b1_okafor_herrera__r4, b2_thornbury_lim__r3 x1 each; c1_against_stereotype and case2_negotiation x2; unseen2_feedback x1) - runtime_metrics.json reports only the integer, never who, when or why; 1 group-observation downgrade in c1_against_stereotype where code rewrote the world's observed=true to false; and every firing of the MIN_STEP_ON_A_CROWDED_INSTANT floor - 23 instants across the corpus sit at exactly MAX_EVENTS_PER_INSTANT=3 (e.g. artifacts/matched_pairs/b2_thornbury_lim journal.jsonl has three events at 2026-09-08T08:00:00 then three at 08:01:00; c1_against_stereotype has six such instants) and nothing in the record distinguishes a timestamp the world judged from one code floored.
findings.why_it_matters: The governing claim is that code owns time and the LLMs own meaning. Every place where code silently overrode the model's answer - floored a duration, deleted a proposed event as a duplicate, destroyed an event after two failed reviews, downgraded a group observation, threw away a whole turn - is unrecorded in the persisted artifacts, so no external reviewer can measure how much of the trajectory is the model's judgment and how much is a constant. It also means the abandoned-turn reasons, which are the clearest signal of where the continuity review is misfiring, are lost after the run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the six kinds to write_artifacts as a single code_overrides.jsonl (or fold them into the existing per-topic files) so every code override of a model answer is in the record.

findings.title: MAX_INTENTIONS_PER_TURN=3 is undisclosed to the actor and enforced by destroying the whole reply, so the constant reaches into what the person believes
findings.evidence: actor_mind.py:33 sets the cap; actor_mind.py:156-159 raises ActorResponseError on the whole response, which llm.py:150-190 retries once and trajectory.py:454-470 turns into an abandoned turn on a second failure. ACTOR_SYSTEM (actor_mind.py:36-121) never states the cap - it says only 'If you attempt more than one thing, they must be genuinely different things.' It fired three times live, in all three cases on the same four-step task: artifacts/matched_pairs/b2_thornbury_lim__r3 c24, b1_okafor_herrera__r4 c21, b1_okafor_herrera__r2 c12, each listing print / sign / scan / email the lease. In b1_okafor_herrera__r2 c12 the rejected reply also carried private_updates: ["The lease terms are acceptable, as expected."]; the accepted retry carries private_updates: [] - a code constant about how many actions may be attempted deleted a belief the person had formed.
findings.why_it_matters: The cap is defended in its own comment as a budget boundary, which is legitimate, but it is enforced by rejecting the entire response rather than by bounding what the runtime will act on. Because the model rewrites everything on retry, the number changes the decision text and the private memory as well as the action count, and it costs two provider calls every time a person genuinely has a four-step task. MAX_PRIVATE_UPDATES_PER_TURN=6 and MAX_WAKES_PER_JUDGMENT=4 have the same undisclosed-hard-reject shape and have simply not fired yet.
findings.suggested_fix: State the caps in ACTOR_SYSTEM and WORLD_SYSTEM, and/or truncate to the first N with a persisted note instead of rejecting the whole reply.

findings.title: MAX_ENV_CHAIN=1 abandons the world's own declared unfinished business with nothing scheduled and nobody consulted
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:538 sets MAX_ENV_CHAIN=1. In _after_commit, the not-follow_up branch (trajectory.py:643-668) resets the depth AND hands the turn back to the doer via actor_step(self_act_of) at :666-667. The chain-cut branch (trajectory.py:669-671) does neither: it resets the depth and returns, so on a second consecutive follow_up=true event nothing further is asked of the world, no wake is scheduled to compensate, and self_act_of is not consulted. 177 of the 522 events proposed across the corpus carried follow_up=true.
findings.why_it_matters: follow_up=true is the world stating in its own words that this event leaves something in transit or underway. When the depth bound trips, that transit is dropped silently - and because the branch skips the doer's turn as well, the person who set it in motion is not brought back either. In a run whose queue is otherwise empty this is another route to a step-1 stop and a defaulted NO. Unlike the not-follow_up path the asymmetry is not explained in the comment.
findings.suggested_fix: On the chain cut, either hand the turn back to self_act_of as the finished branch does, or schedule one wake for the affected actor so the unfinished thing is picked up later.

findings.title: ActorGroundingError and EventGroundingError are declared with full docstrings and never raised
findings.evidence: sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trajectory.py:39-43 and :45-47 define both classes. A repo-wide grep finds exactly one other occurrence of either name: the except tuple at trajectory.py:963. Neither is raised anywhere in the runtime, the tests, or the evaluation scripts.
findings.why_it_matters: Their docstrings describe a behaviour ('one targeted correction did not fix it. Nothing is committed, and code does not invent a replacement decision') that is in fact implemented elsewhere and differently - as an abandoned turn (trajectory.py:462-470) and an abandoned event (trajectory.py:301-310), neither of which raises. A reader auditing the failure modes from the exception vocabulary gets a false picture of how grounding failures are handled.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete both classes and remove them from the except tuple at trajectory.py:963.

findings.title: Undisclosed history windows: the event reviewer is asked to detect repetition while seeing only the last 12 events
findings.evidence: journal.render_for_world defaults to limit=60 (journal.py:163); trajectory.py:386 passes limit=12 for the event-quality review. EVENT_REVIEW_SYSTEM (world_mind.py:333) instructs REVISE for 'something already in the record, in the same or different words', and world_mind.py:246-253 backs it with an exact casefold string match over the full journal. artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation (40 events) and artifacts/matched_pairs/c1_against_stereotype (33 events) both exceed the 12-event window; unseen2_feedback commits e250 / e256 / e270 ('The email from Aline to Ravi, containing her comments on the thesis chapter, arrives in Ravi's inbox' and two rewordings, pairwise similarity 0.88-0.94) which the exact-match guard cannot see and which the reviewer passed.
findings.why_it_matters: Two code-chosen numbers govern how much history each semantic role can reason about, neither is disclosed anywhere in the artifacts, and the 12 is small enough that the repetition criterion the reviewer is given cannot be applied to anything older. The 60 has not yet bound - no completed run exceeds 40 committed events - but nothing records when it does, so a longer run would silently start hiding history from the world.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the applied window in the world/review exchange entries, and raise or remove the 12 so the repetition check can see what it is asked about.

findings.title: 4,268 lines of superseded compiler - including a 905-line capability ontology and a world graph - ship alongside the runtime
findings.evidence: compiler/legacy/ contains capabilities.py (905 lines), assembly.py (579), graph_builder.py (432), validation.py (400), pipeline.py (360), translation.py (335), world_graph.py (143) and others, totalling 4,268 lines against 1,543 for the production compiler and 3,184 for the whole semantic runtime. It is properly quarantined - compiler/__init__.py does not import it, the only reachable path is compile_question.py:62-68 behind an explicit --compiler legacy flag, and all 16 files are hash-frozen in artifacts/semantic_runtime/COMPILER_FREEZE.txt.
findings.why_it_matters: This is not a live second compiler and I could not find any production path to it, so it is not a design violation. It is dead weight, and it is dead weight of exactly the shape the design forbids - a capability menu, an action ontology and a second world representation - sitting one import away in the same package as the frozen production compiler.
findings.suggested_fix: Move compiler/legacy/ out of the shipped package into a clearly archival location, or delete it and keep the comparison in git history.

findings.title: Required inventory: every numeric constant in the runtime, with verdict - none is a number deciding how people behave
findings.evidence: trajectory.py: MAX_EVENTS_PER_INSTANT=3 (:56) time-granularity guard, ALLOWED, counts both committed and already-scheduled events at the instant (:246-251) so it cannot be evaded, and it binds correctly - no instant in the corpus exceeds 3. MIN_STEP_ON_A_CROWDED_INSTANT=1min (:57) ALLOWED, applied only when the model said 'now' on a full instant (:343), pure clock bookkeeping. MAX_ENV_CHAIN=1 (:538) recursion bound, ALLOWED but see the MEDIUM above. MAX_WORLD_RUN=6 (:548) bound on consecutive world calls without a person speaking, ALLOWED - it only ever causes MORE people to be consulted, never fewer. max_steps default 60 / 250 in run_simulation.py (:127) ALLOWED, hitting it yields truncated=True and status 'incomplete', never a converted NO (:940-947, :769-789). budget_for arithmetic (:80-85) ALLOWED, derived from the structural caps rather than picked. actor_mind.py: MAX_INTENTIONS_PER_TURN=3 (:33) and MAX_PRIVATE_UPDATES_PER_TURN=6 (:34) budget boundaries - ALLOWED in intent, see the MEDIUM above on enforcement. envelope.py: MAX_WAKES_PER_JUDGMENT=4 (:44), MAX_TEXT_CHARS=2000 (:50), MAX_STEP_DAYS=30 (:100) and the _UNITS table (:84-88) - all ALLOWED, universal time/size bookkeeping. llm.py: SOCKET_TIMEOUT_S=90, TOTAL_READ_DEADLINE_S=240, TOTAL_REQUEST_DEADLINE_S=270, MAX_RETRIES_PER_CALL=1, MAX_REJECTION_ECHO=500, MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES=4MiB, RESERVED_FINAL_CALLS=2, max_calls=400, temperature=0.7, max_tokens=1200 - all ALLOWED, transport and provider parameters. journal.py: render_for_world limit 60/12 - ALLOWED, see the LOW above. Runtime counters: news / news_at_turn (trajectory.py:143-144) are used only as a change-detector (news > news_at_turn, :552), never as a magnitude against a threshold; since_actor['n'] and env_chain['depth'] are compared only against the ceilings above. Every one of the 15 comparisons in trajectory.py (:197, 201, 251, 350, 552, 605, 633, 669, 769, 823, 825, 836, 854, 903, 940) is a clock ordering, a change-detector, a cardinality test (len(for)>1, 'is this a group'), or a counter against a technical ceiling. No model-supplied number is ever compared against a threshold, and no constant expresses a behavioural assumption.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the inventory my brief required rather than a defect. The central prohibition - no arbitrary numerical variable may control social behaviour - holds in this runtime, and it holds structurally rather than by accident: nothing numeric the model writes is ever read back as a number. Recorded so the next reviewer can diff against it.
findings.suggested_fix: No change required; keep this inventory alongside RUNTIME_FREEZE.txt so any new constant has to be justified against it.
